text:
pagerduty-bot: 🔔 ALERT: SLO breach detected
Alert: p99 latency > 1200ms for /v1/generate (streaming + batching path)
Service: inference-runtime-prod
Policy: realtime-slo-800ms
Triggered at 2025-11-09T03:46:29Z (ts: 1953456789)

mike_oncall: acked. jumping in. looking at dashboards now.

mike_oncall: grafana: p95 ~ 350ms but p99 spikes to 1.2s+, sudden in last 7m. traces show many streaming requests stuck in batch queue.

sara_sre: same, I'm seeing queue_length spike on batcher-v2 pods and batch_size distribution shifted right (lots of 128/256 batches). probably mixed seq-length packing causing stalls.

jordan_runtime: confirmed. continuous-batching path (#cbatcher) has a longer pack window for streaming to maximize throughput; looks like a regression in the fairness scheduler patch from yesterday.

lee_prodops: any customer impact? cs-rep: we got a ticket from AcmeAnalytics about degraded interactive latency since ~03:40 UTC. two other customers flagged anomalies.

mike_oncall: impact: 3 paying customers intermittently seeing p99>1s for streaming endpoints. not total outage but SLO breached. marking Sev3/4 depending on SLA tier. paging followups to CS.

sara_sre: immediate mitigation options:
- reduce max batch size to 32 for streaming route
- temporarily disable continuous batching for streaming requests (fall back to immediate dispatch)
- bump scheduler fairness to favor small seq requests (weight change)

mike_oncall: let's do the fastest low-risk change first: set MAX_BATCH_SIZE=32 on batcher-v2 for the streaming route via admin endpoint. if that doesn't help, disable continuous mode.

jordan_runtime: applying config now. command:```bash
curl -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN\" \"https://admin.internal/redwood/batcher/v2/config\" -d '{"routes":{"/v1/generate_stream":{"max_batch_size":32}}}'
```

deploy-bot: config-change: batcher-v2 route /v1/generate_stream max_batch_size -> 32 by jordan_runtime at 2025-11-09T03:49:12Z

mike_oncall: watching metrics. queue_length dropping, p99 fell from 1.2s -> 680ms within two minutes. good sign.

sara_sre: still seeing occasional 1s tail spikes correlated with single large-seq requests being stuck at head-of-queue (head-of-line blocking). need scheduler-level preemption or KV cache eviction to avoid long head times.

jordan_runtime: quick additional mitigation: enable preemptive-shedding for requests exceeding seq_len 2048 on streaming route. admin command:```json
{
  "routes":{
    "/v1/generate_stream":{
      "preempt_threshold_seq_len":2048,
      "enable_preempt":true
    }
  }
}
```
(I'll apply after we confirm p99 improving)

mike_oncall: CS on the thread: cs-rep please notify AcmeAnalytics that we're mitigating and will follow up with RCA. include ETA for full fix ~2-4 hours.

cs-rep: pinged AcmeAnalytics (via email + support portal). they acknowledged. said interactive UI is sluggish but still usable. asking for updates.

sara_sre: note: telemetry shows mixed sequence length distribution change at 03:38 — likely a customer workload change that interacted badly with our new fairness scheduling. patch introduced yesterday didn't consider extreme long sequences. filing bug.

mike_oncall: ok, plan for next 60m:
1) observe for 15m after max_batch_size change (in progress)
2) if p99 remains >800ms: disable continuous batching for streaming route and route to immediate-dispatch path
3) if still bad: divert traffic for affected customers to dedicated nodes or lower-latency model variant (fallback small model)
4) postmortem owner: jordan_runtime (will coordinate with sara_sre)

jordan_runtime: noted. I'll own the postmortem and schedule a follow-up with SRE + runtime. linking issue: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RT-4521

mike_oncall: metrics at 03:53 UTC: p99 down to 480ms, p95 stable at 320ms, queue length normalized. looks like change helped.

deploy-bot: rollout: feature-flag continuous-batching-fairness reverted by deploy-bot at 2025-11-09T03:55:01Z (rollback commit 7a1b3c).

sara_sre: confirm rollback happened. need to add automated tests for mixed seq-length behavior.

lee_prodops: any need to rotate capacity or scale up nodes? jordan_runtime: not yet, system headroom fine after change. will reopen if needed.

mike_oncall: next on-call handoff to jordan_runtime at 04:15 UTC. Jordan, take over monitoring and action if p99 creeps back above 800ms.

jordan_runtime: taking handoff early at 03:58 UTC. I'll monitor for 2 hours and own the RCA. initial mitigation remains: max_batch_size=32 + rollback of fairness change.

mike_oncall: documenting incident for postmortem. I'll annotate timeline + customer impact. sliding severity to Sev3 resolved -> monitoring.

cs-rep: updated tickets for the three customers with mitigation details and expected RCA timeline.

sara_sre: follow-ups for RCA:
- reproduce workload locally with mixed seq lengths and fairness patch
- add unit/integration tests for scheduler behavior with extreme long sequences
- consider adding head-of-line preemption or per-request latency budget enforcement
- evaluate making continuous-batching opt-in for streaming routes

mike_oncall: thanks everyone. closing page. tagging incident owner jordan_runtime and RCA due in 72 hours.

jordan_runtime: will post RCA draft in incidents channel and ping for review.

pagerduty-bot: ALERT cleared for incident 1953456789 at 2025-11-09T04:01:45Z

mike_oncall: closing thread, handing off active monitoring to jordan_runtime. :white_check_mark:
